name: Untertilliach
kurzbeschreibung: Tiny, secluded village in the upper Gailtal, with authentic nature and absolute tranquility.
beschreibung:
Overview

Untertilliach is situated at an elevation of 1,235 meters in the Tyrolean section of the Lesachtal within East Tyrol's Lienz district, nestled in a dramatic high-altitude trough between the rugged Carnic Alps to the south and the Gailtal Alps and Lienz Dolomites to the north. Home to approximately 220 residents, this peaceful mountain community spans from the shaded valley floor of the Gail River up to steep hillside hamlets such as Eggen at 1,800 meters. To the east, the valley borders Carinthia near the renowned pilgrimage village of Maria Luggau. Untertilliach ranks among the most pristine and unspoiled alpine valleys in Europe: as part of the international Mountaineering Villages (Bergsteigerdörfer) network, it champions sustainable, tranquil tourism without mechanical ski lifts, shaped by sun-bleached timber farmsteads, steep alpine hay meadows, and enduring agricultural crafts.

History

Celtic and Venetic traces endure in the archaic field names of the high valley, which served as a secure haven during late antiquity and the Migration Period. Between 1075 and 1090, properties were transferred to the Prince-Bishopric of Brixen, before the Counts of Görz systematically cleared the terrain for alpine dairy estates ('Schwaighöfe'). An enduring landmark is the ancient filial Church of Saint Jenewein on the Kirchberg: consecrated in Gothic style in 1479 atop a panoramic ridge at 1,370 meters, it served as the valley's primary parish center until 1870. To ease perilous winter ascents, the Baroque Parish Church of Saints Florian, Ingenuin, and Albuin was built on the valley floor between 1777 and 1780, its distinctive neo-Baroque double onion dome tower completed in 1891. The valley is internationally renowned for its milling heritage: nearly every farmstead operated a water-powered wooden mill along mountain torrents to grind grain for traditional Lesachtal rye bread, recognized by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage since 2010.

Getting There

By car, travel from the north or west along the Drautal Federal Road B100 to Tassenbach, then follow the Gailtal Road B111 through Kartitsch and Obertilliach to Untertilliach (about 20 kilometers). From Carinthia, the B111 winds through Kötschach-Mauthen across the Lesachtal. Rail passengers arrive at Tassenbach or Sillian stations on the Puster Valley Railway. From there, regular regional bus line 965 operates between Tassenbach, Obertilliach, Untertilliach, and Maria Luggau.

Tips

A memorable cultural hike ascends from the valley floor to the historic hillside church of Saint Jenewein on the Kirchberg, providing magnificent vistas of the Carnic crests. Seasoned trekkers can access the Carnic High Trail (Friedensweg 403), tracing the historic ridge along the Italian frontier. Just five kilometers east in Maria Luggau, visitors can walk the famous Mill Path, observing working historic waterwheels and traditional baking demonstrations of authentic stone-ground Lesachtal bread. In winter, Untertilliach offers tranquil snowshoeing and ski mountaineering far from crowded slopes.
